note: Music section, 14-day window. Note: window_hours('2026-08-14T22:05:00Z') returns the design default 72 when called without a section arg, so 336 (music) is set explicitly here — every item was gated with `python3 pipeline/freshness.py <published_iso> 2026-08-14T22:05:00Z music` and printed FRESH. Published times were read from each article page (og article:published_time / JSON-LD datePublished / visible byline date) via WebFetch, never from search snippets. Where a page exposed only a relative date ('1 day ago', '4 days ago', '8 days ago' on musictech.com) the ISO was derived from now_iso and the time-of-day set to a conservative midday value; those items sit far inside the 336h window either way. Sources swept via section indexes/RSS rather than search snippets (search results skewed heavily stale): musictech.com (news, news/gear, news/industry), musicradar.com/news/tech, gearnews.com (+ /tag/ai/), bedroomproducersblog.com, synthtopia.com, cdm.link (+ /tag/ai/), kvraudio.com/news, hypebot.com, musicbusinessworldwide.com, midiaresearch.com/blog, soundonsound.com/news, attackmagazine.com/news, djmag.com/tech, completemusicupdate.com, engadget.com, techcrunch.com, factmag.com. Keyword expansion beyond keywords_music.json: BMG/Kobalt publisher licensing, EU AI Act labelling, AI-assisted plugin development (Audio Plugin Coder, AI-coded synths), 'anti-banger' data-poisoning music, Rust DAW with native AI sample generation, AI vinyl pressing, creator-survey data on AI acceptance, 'why no AI hit yet'. Blocked/dead for our user agent: theverge.com and pitchfork.com (WebSearch rejects them), digitalmusicnews.com (403 on both category and article pages), billboard.com + rollingstone.com (307 -> tollbit paywall, 402), music-ally.com (redirects to linkfire.com), residentadvisor.net/ra.co and mixmag.net (403 / JS-only), waterandmusic.com (archive gated), youtube.com channel pages returned no video listings so social contributed nothing. Dropped as STALE after real-date verification: musicradar Roland Melody Flip (2026-03-18), musicradar Google/ProducerAI (2026-02-25), musicradar prompts-to-plugins feature (2026-06-26), musicradar FL Studio agentic chatbot (2026-07-10), musictech Moises AI Studio (2025-08-20), musictech Udio Styles (2025-04-03), musictech Splice x ElevenLabs (2026-05-19), musictech Fender Studio Pro 8.1 (2026-06-10), attackmagazine FL Studio 2026 (2026-07-09), attackmagazine PEEL STEMS 2 (2026-07-08), attackmagazine Yamaha Creator Pass (2026-06-30), kvraudio TonalBrain Mix (2026-06-08), djmag Gemini/Lyria 3 (2026-02-20), MBW Vocalist AI (2024-04-08). Dropped as AI-business noise with no design/creative hook: MBW Ticketmaster-in-Gemini, engadget DeepSeek pricing, techcrunch Anthropic watermarking, musictech InMusic/Native Instruments UK shutdown. Overlap warning for the curator: items 1, 3, 12 and 14 are four outlets on the same Suno x BMG licensing story — pick at most one. items.title: Suno x BMG: AI music platform strikes its second major label licensing deal
items.excerpt: Suno has signed a global licensing deal with BMG covering both recorded and publishing repertoire, its second major-label agreement after Warner. Universal and Sony are still pursuing legal action against the platform.

items.title: Suno Vinyl: press your AI-generated music to a real 12-inch record
items.excerpt: Suno is launching a vinyl pressing service that turns a user's generated tracklist into a custom 12-inch with a designed sleeve, around $45 per record. It pushes prompt-made music into a physical, collectible object.

items.title: AI's ties to major labels deepen as Suno strikes licensing deal with BMG
items.excerpt: Suno has reached an agreement with BMG to build AI models trained on licensed music, with participating artists and songwriters compensated. It precedes Suno's first generative model developed in partnership with the industry.

items.title: Music to confuse AI might be the next new genre
items.excerpt: Artists including MattstaGraham and iamriverhawk are deliberately writing 'anti-bangers' — deformed, unconventional tracks made in the hope that AI trains on them. Data poisoning is turning into an actual creative practice.

items.title: OA-Labs releases Phosphor-1, a FREE unstable analog-style synth for macOS
items.excerpt: A designer-musician built this free virtual-analog synth in about two months using AI to write the code, spending the saved time on the interface and the sound. Its 'Age' knob drifts pitch, filter, level and shape together.

items.title: Noizefield updates Audio Plugin Coder to v1.4.0 — JUCE 9 support, guided setup and AI workflow commands
items.excerpt: Audio Plugin Coder is an open-source framework that turns a natural-language plugin concept into a buildable VST3/AU project using AI agents. v1.4.0 adds JUCE 9.0.1 support, a setup wizard and dedicated AI workflow commands.

items.title: Where artists draw the line on AI: Uppbeat Creator Report
items.excerpt: A survey of nearly 1,800 creative professionals found only 6.7% accept fully AI-generated content, while roughly 60% welcome AI as a collaborator. It maps where creators actually draw the assist-versus-replace line.

items.title: The era of unlabeled AI content in Europe is ending
items.excerpt: The EU AI Act's transparency rules mean AI-generated content should no longer be anonymous, requiring disclosure when audio, images, video or text are machine-made or manipulated. Music creators get new labelling obligations.

items.title: Spotify has roped indie publisher Kobalt into its AI platform for covers and remixes
items.excerpt: Spotify signed Kobalt for its forthcoming AI covers-and-remixes tool, a paid Premium add-on that lets fans generate their own versions of licensed songs. Participating writers get an extra royalty line.

items.title: After Universal and Merlin deals, Spotify inks agreement with Kobalt for AI-powered fan-made covers and remixes
items.excerpt: Kobalt is the first publisher outside Universal to license Spotify's fan-facing AI remix tool. Spotify's Charlie Hellman frames it as 'grounded in consent, credit, and compensation for the songwriters who take part'.

items.title: Suno inks global licensing deal with BMG
items.excerpt: Suno's agreement with BMG covers recorded and publishing repertoire worldwide, following its Warner deal nine months earlier. Artists and songwriters must opt in before their work feeds the models.

items.title: Suno forms 'global alliance' with BMG giving musicians 'real choice' over AI use
items.excerpt: The partnership sets out opt-in protections and compensation for artists and marks Suno's first model developed with the industry rather than around it. Legal challenges elsewhere in the sector continue.

items.title: Suno CEO insists Suno is 'responsible' and isn't going to leave people behind
items.excerpt: Mikey Shulman says watermarking and download limits are coming as Suno tries to hold the line between democratising music creation and enabling copyright abuse. The pitch is AI that widens who gets to make music.

items.title: Daft Punk's Thomas Bangalter explains why he's 'not interested in the creative use of AI'
items.excerpt: Bangalter argues the meaningful part of making music is non-verbal and emotional, not describable in a prompt: 'we can't have technology do that for us.' A pointed counterweight to prompt-first tooling.

items.title: Beatport bans AI-generated music
items.excerpt: Beatport is extending its Beatdapp partnership to block fully or majority AI-generated tracks while still allowing AI-assisted work where a human is the primary creator, after 77% of its DJ community backed supporting human artists.
